instruments.title: EBK quantisation — the semiclassical prediction against the exact spectrum

inputs.name: beta_plus
inputs.doc: anisotropy coordinate beta_+. At zero anisotropy the top is spherical, every level is degenerate and there is no torus structure to quantise

inputs.name: beta_minus
inputs.doc: anisotropy coordinate beta_-

inputs.name: levels
inputs.doc: how many EBK tori to compute, each compared against its own exact doublet

inputs.name: quadrature
inputs.doc: samples in the action integral. The quadrature error is separate from the semiclassical error and must be pushed below it before any convergence rate can be read

outputs.name: c
outputs.doc: the three sorted inverse squared axis lengths that define the top

outputs.name: L
outputs.doc: the Langer length j + 1/2 used as the classical angular momentum

outputs.name: levels
outputs.doc: per torus: the EBK energy, the exact doublet mean it is compared against, the tunnelling splitting, the relative error, and whether that splitting is above the double-precision floor

outputs.name: worst_relative_error
outputs.doc: the largest disagreement with a doublet mean over the levels computed

instruments.title: Particle creation — what an anisotropic universe makes, and what expansion does not

inputs.name: beta_plus
inputs.doc: anisotropy coordinate beta_+; zero with beta_- gives exactly zero created particles

inputs.name: beta_minus
inputs.doc: anisotropy coordinate beta_-

inputs.name: p_plus
inputs.doc: momentum conjugate to beta_+

inputs.name: p_minus
inputs.doc: momentum conjugate to beta_-

inputs.name: Lambda
inputs.doc: the cosmological term

inputs.name: j
inputs.doc: which spin block the mode lives in

inputs.name: level
inputs.doc: which level within the block, counted from the lowest. The adiabatic labelling of a level fails at a level crossing, and a crossing is not detected here

inputs.name: tauMax
inputs.doc: integration window in volume time

outputs.name: n
outputs.doc: the occupation |B|^2 of ONE mode in the adiabatic vacuum at tau = 0 — not a total particle number, and carrying no sum over the (2j+1)^2 degeneracy or over j

outputs.doc: worst |A|^2 - |B|^2 - 1 along the run. Never projected back, so it measures the integration honestly

outputs.name: alpha_growth

outputs.name: stop
outputs.doc: window, collapse, overflow, de Sitter escape or step budget

outputs.name: steps
outputs.doc: adaptive steps taken

outputs.name: seed_rescaled
outputs.doc: 1 unless the requested momenta were off the constraint surface and had to be scaled onto it

instruments.title: Spectral operator — H(t) = ½ Σ a_i⁻² K_i² on an anisotropic S³

inputs.name: alpha
inputs.doc: the logarithmic scale factor of the Bianchi IX geometry the operator is evaluated on

inputs.name: beta_plus
inputs.doc: anisotropy coordinate beta_+; zero with beta_- gives the round sphere

inputs.name: beta_minus
inputs.doc: anisotropy coordinate beta_-; zero alone leaves c1 = c2, an axially symmetric top

inputs.name: j_max
inputs.doc: highest half-integer spin block to diagonalise for the level list; the lowest level and the gap are always taken over j ≤ 2, where they live, whatever is asked here. Blocks are (2j+1)-dimensional and the cost is cubic in that, so this is the only knob that costs anything

outputs.name: c
outputs.doc: the three inverse squared scale factors that define the top

outputs.name: lowest
outputs.doc: the lowest eigenvalue over all blocks

outputs.name: gap
outputs.doc: the spacing between the lowest two DISTINCT levels. Computed from the metric at one instant and never inferred from the classical dynamics

outputs.name: distinct
outputs.doc: every distinct eigenvalue with its FULL multiplicity, spectator index included

outputs.name: blocks
outputs.doc: per spin j: the eigenvalues of the (2j+1)-dimensional block, its spectator multiplicity, and the total (2j+1)^2

outputs.name: trace_residual
outputs.doc: how far the assembled spectrum is from the exact trace identity, recomputed live rather than quoted — a broken build says so instead of returning plausible numbers

outputs.name: level_count
outputs.doc: distinct levels and total states, so the degeneracy structure is visible at a glance

instruments.title: Bianchi IX — constraint-preserving evolution and trajectory class

inputs.name: alpha
inputs.doc: the logarithmic scale factor

inputs.name: beta_plus
inputs.doc: anisotropy coordinate beta_+

inputs.name: beta_minus
inputs.doc: anisotropy coordinate beta_-

inputs.name: p_plus
inputs.doc: momentum conjugate to beta_+

inputs.name: p_minus
inputs.doc: momentum conjugate to beta_-

inputs.name: Lambda
inputs.doc: the cosmological term. Vacuum Bianchi IX with Lambda has NO equilibrium: p_alpha stationarity forces exp(2*alpha) = 1/(4*Lambda) while the constraint forces 3/(4*Lambda)

inputs.name: branch
inputs.doc: which root of the constraint the initial momentum takes

inputs.name: tauMax
inputs.doc: integration window in volume time

outputs.name: class
outputs.doc: one of stationary, periodic, quasiperiodic, chaotic, transient, singular, unreachable

outputs.name: lyapunov
outputs.doc: Benettin estimate over the DOUBLED window, driven by the exact Jacobian of the flow. null for any run that is not bounded, because on a de Sitter escape the tangent grows with the inflating background and not with any sensitivity

outputs.name: lyapunov_doubling_ratio
outputs.doc: lambda(2T)/lambda(T). A regular orbit decays like ln(tau)/tau so this tends to 0.5 + ln2/(2 ln T); a chaotic one plateaus and it tends to 1. This ratio, not a threshold on lambda, is what decides the chaotic class

outputs.name: lyapunov_expected_if_regular
outputs.doc: what the ratio would be for a regular orbit at this window, so the measurement can be read against its own null hypothesis

outputs.name: lyapunov_verdict
outputs.doc: plateau, decaying, or not measured — in words

outputs.name: constraint_residual
outputs.doc: |H_tau| normalised by the CURRENT scale of its own terms, not the initial one

outputs.name: bounces
outputs.doc: curvature-wall reflections counted during the run

outputs.name: stop
outputs.doc: why integration ended: window, collapse, overflow or de Sitter escape

outputs.name: steps
outputs.doc: adaptive Dormand-Prince 5(4) steps taken

outputs.name: seed_rescaled
outputs.doc: 1 unless the requested momenta were off the constraint surface and had to be scaled onto it — reported rather than applied silently

outputs.name: alpha_final
outputs.doc: the logarithmic scale factor the trajectory reached, ready to be routed into the spectral operator, particle creation or EBK

outputs.name: beta_plus_final
outputs.doc: the anisotropy β₊ the trajectory reached

outputs.name: beta_minus_final
outputs.doc: the anisotropy β₋ the trajectory reached

outputs.name: p_plus_final
outputs.doc: the momentum conjugate to β₊ at the end of the run

outputs.name: p_minus_final
outputs.doc: the momentum conjugate to β₋ at the end of the run

outputs.name: tau_final
outputs.doc: the volume time actually reached, which is less than tauMax whenever the run stopped early

outputs.doc: and the difference, which is the arithmetic and not the physics

inputs.doc: where in the cell to compare the lattice with solid-body rotation, as a fraction of the radius

inputs.name: angular_samples
inputs.doc: how finely to average the velocity around that circle. The field has a 1/d singularity at every line, so this is quadrature and its error is measured rather than assumed

outputs.name: kappa
outputs.doc: the circulation quantum in use

outputs.name: kappa_helium4
outputs.doc: h/m for helium four: 9.9693e-8

outputs.name: kappa_helium3
outputs.doc: h/2m for helium three, where the pairs carry twice the mass and the quantum is smaller

outputs.name: flux_quantum
outputs.doc: h/2e = 2.067833848e-15 Wb, and it is EXACT: both h and e are SI defining constants, so this is not a measurement of anything

outputs.name: vortex_density
outputs.doc: 2 Omega / kappa, Feynman

outputs.name: flux_density
outputs.doc: B / Phi_0, Abrikosov — the same formula for the charged case

outputs.name: rotation_per_tesla
outputs.doc: the exchange rate between the two mechanisms: 2.41e7 radians per second buys what one tesla buys. This is why vortex lattices are photographed in superconductors and only heroically in helium

outputs.name: lattice_spacing
outputs.doc: the triangular spacing at that density

outputs.name: omega_c1
outputs.doc: the rotation at which the first vortex becomes favourable in this cell

outputs.name: lines_in_cell
outputs.doc: how many lines the lattice actually placed inside the cell

outputs.name: lines_enclosed
outputs.doc: and how many are inside the sampling circle — an INTEGER, which is the whole point

outputs.name: lines_expected
outputs.doc: n pi r^2, the continuum count it is supposed to approximate, which is not an integer

outputs.name: v_measured
outputs.doc: the azimuthal velocity the lattice actually produces there, summed over every line

outputs.name: v_ampere
outputs.doc: kappa N / (2 pi r) from the enclosed integer

outputs.name: v_solid_body
outputs.doc: Omega r, what a rigid bucket of water would do

outputs.name: ampere_residual
outputs.doc: |v_measured / v_ampere - 1|. Ampere is EXACT for line vortices, so this is quadrature error and it falls by orders of magnitude with angular_samples

outputs.name: solid_body_ratio
outputs.doc: v_measured / Omega r. A rotating superfluid is NOT rigid; it is rigid on average over many vortices

outputs.name: counting_fluctuation
outputs.doc: |N - n pi r^2| / (n pi r^2). This is what the departure from solid body IS, and the two agree to three digits

outputs.name: ring_speed
outputs.doc: Kelvin: the self-induced speed of a vortex ring of the cell radius. The logarithm is why a big ring is SLOWER than a small one

instruments.title: The cosmological constant, as a length — and the horizon that is four horizons

inputs.name: hubble_constant
inputs.doc: H0. The distance ladder of this atlas declares the same number and this laboratory recomputes rather than imports it, so the two can disagree

inputs.name: omega_lambda
inputs.doc: the dark-energy density parameter. The capacity selector declares this and the distance ladder declares a matter density of 0.3111; that they sum to one is checked and is not assumed

inputs.name: lambda_override
inputs.doc: a cosmological constant from anywhere in this atlas. Zero means: compute it from H0 and Omega_L. Four publications carry this unit and until now nothing consumed one

outputs.name: lambda
outputs.doc: the cosmological constant in use

outputs.name: de_sitter_radius
outputs.doc: sqrt(3/Lambda): the LENGTH the universe has, in the same sense that a black hole has a Schwarzschild radius

outputs.name: de_sitter_gly
outputs.doc: the same in billions of light years: 17.41

outputs.name: hubble_length_gly
outputs.doc: c/H0 = 14.45 Gly, which is a DIFFERENT length and is often called the same thing

outputs.name: de_sitter_over_hubble
outputs.doc: their ratio, which must be exactly 1/sqrt(Omega_L). It is an identity and it is the check that the two lengths are one cosmology. It is NOT called `radius_ratio`: this atlas measured the cost of generic coordinate names one release ago and named this one generically anyway, whereupon the bus proposed a coupling into an accretion disk`s radius ratio. Third time

outputs.name: horizon_area
outputs.doc: the area of the de Sitter horizon, 4piL² — a quarter of it in Planck units is the entropy the cosmological constant carries

outputs.name: horizon_entropy
outputs.doc: one quarter of that area in Planck units

outputs.name: horizon_bits
outputs.doc: and in bits: 4.7e122 for the de Sitter horizon

outputs.name: hubble_bits
outputs.doc: 3.2e122 for the Hubble sphere, which is what this atlas already quoted for `the observable universe`

outputs.name: particle_bits
outputs.doc: 3.4e123 for the light cone, which is what most people mean by observable

outputs.name: horizon_spread
outputs.doc: the ratio between the largest and smallest of those three. It is ten, and a number quoted to two figures with an ambiguity of ten is not a measurement

outputs.name: gibbons_hawking_K
outputs.doc: hbar c / 2 pi k L = 2.2e-30 kelvin, the coldest temperature anything in physics has

outputs.name: vacuum_density
outputs.doc: Lambda c^2 / 8 pi G

outputs.name: vacuum_energy_density
outputs.doc: the same in joules per cubic metre: about half a nanojoule

outputs.name: planck_density
outputs.doc: c^5 / hbar G^2

outputs.name: planck_ratio
outputs.doc: their ratio: 1.15e-123. This is the cosmological constant problem and it is a division

outputs.name: orders_of_magnitude
outputs.doc: its logarithm, -122.94, which is the number everybody quotes as `a hundred and twenty-something`

outputs.name: lambda_planck_units
outputs.doc: Lambda times the Planck area: 2.89e-122. The same problem stated as a dimensionless number rather than as a ratio of densities, and it is a different number by a factor of exactly 8 pi = 25.13 -- the one Einstein put in front of the stress tensor, since rho_vac carries a 1/8 pi G that the Planck density does not

outputs.name: flatness_residual
outputs.doc: |Omega_L + Omega_m - 1| using the matter density the distance ladder declares. Two constants typed in two files, and this is the gate that says they still agree

instruments.title: Where the elements came from — three minutes, ten billion years, and one second

inputs.name: freeze_out_temperature
inputs.doc: kT at which the weak interaction stops keeping neutrons and protons in equilibrium. It is QUOTED — deriving it needs the weak rates against the expansion rate, which this laboratory does not do — and the helium fraction is very sensitive to it: 0.7 gives 20 per cent and 0.9 gives 29

inputs.name: deuterium_delay
inputs.doc: how long free neutrons decay before deuterium stops being photodisintegrated and nucleosynthesis can begin. The deuterium bottleneck is why this is minutes rather than seconds: the binding energy is only 2.2 MeV and there are two billion photons per baryon

inputs.name: capture_time
inputs.doc: how long a nucleus waits for the next neutron. A thousand years in a dying giant`s helium shell, ten microseconds a second after two neutron stars touch

inputs.name: beta_time
inputs.doc: and how long it waits to beta-decay. The comparison between these two numbers is the ENTIRE distinction between the s-process and the r-process

inputs.name: environment
inputs.doc: a site to load both times from at once

inputs.name: ladder_step
inputs.doc: how far up the alpha ladder to climb, from helium at zero to nickel-56 at eleven

outputs.name: neutron_proton_difference
outputs.doc: 1.2933 MeV. NOT the 0.7824 that a difference of ATOMIC mass excesses gives — that one is the beta-decay Q-value and includes the electron that leaves. The two are one electron mass apart and using the wrong one gives 41 per cent primordial helium instead of 25, which is not a small error but a different universe

outputs.name: n_over_p_at_freeze
outputs.doc: the Boltzmann factor at freeze-out: about one neutron for every five protons

outputs.name: n_over_p_at_nucleosynthesis
outputs.doc: and after four minutes of free-neutron decay: about one in seven

outputs.name: primordial_helium_fraction
outputs.doc: A QUARTER OF THE MASS OF THE UNIVERSE, from a mass difference, a temperature and a lifetime. Observed: 0.245 plus or minus 0.003. This is one of the three classical tests of the hot big bang and it is three lines of arithmetic

outputs.name: beryllium8_binding
outputs.doc: NEGATIVE: beryllium-8 is unbound by 92 keV and falls apart in eighty attoseconds. Together with the absence of any stable mass-five nucleus this is why the first three minutes stopped at helium — there was no ladder to climb

outputs.name: triple_alpha_q
outputs.doc: 7.2747 MeV, from three helium mass excesses and the zero that DEFINES the atomic mass unit

outputs.name: hoyle_above_threshold
outputs.doc: 0.379 MeV. Fred Hoyle argued in 1953 that carbon could only exist in the observed quantity if there were a resonance just above the three-alpha threshold, and told the experimenters where to look; they found it at 7.654 MeV in 1957. A prediction made from the fact that the predictor was made of carbon

outputs.name: ladder_nucleus
outputs.doc: which nucleus the alpha ladder has reached

outputs.name: ladder_binding_per_nucleon
outputs.doc: and its binding energy per nucleon

outputs.name: ladder_q_this_step
outputs.doc: the energy the last alpha capture released. It stays POSITIVE all the way to nickel-56 even though the binding curve is not monotonic — titanium-44 is less bound per nucleon than calcium-40, because calcium-40 is doubly magic, and the ladder climbs through the dip anyway

outputs.name: most_bound_nucleus
outputs.doc: NICKEL-62, not iron-56. This is the single most commonly misstated fact in the subject: the ranking is Ni-62 at 8.7945 MeV per nucleon, then Fe-58 at 8.7922, then Fe-56 at 8.7903. Iron-56 is the most ABUNDANT end point for a different reason — it is what nickel-56 decays to, and nickel-56 is what a silicon-burning core makes because it has equal protons and neutrons and no time to make anything else

outputs.name: most_bound_per_nucleon
outputs.doc: 8.7945 MeV per nucleon, computed from mass excesses and compared rather than quoted

outputs.name: iron56_deficit
outputs.doc: how far iron-56 falls short of the true peak: 4.2 keV per nucleon. Small enough that calling iron the end of fusion is a good approximation and wrong enough that it is worth knowing it is one

outputs.name: capture_regime
outputs.doc: s or r, from one comparison: does the nucleus capture the next neutron before it beta-decays? A thousand years against ten thousand seconds gives s; ten microseconds against a tenth of a second gives r

outputs.name: capture_ratio
outputs.doc: the ratio of the two times, which is the only number the regime depends on

outputs.name: intermediate_process
outputs.doc: 1 when the two times are within a factor of twenty of each other, where neither name applies. An i-process in that gap is OBSERVED in carbon-enhanced metal-poor stars, and the tidy two-regime story has no room for it

outputs.name: peak_offset_N50
outputs.doc: the s-process abundance peak at neutron number 50 sits at mass 88 and the r-process peak at 80 — EIGHT MASS UNITS APART. The r-process builds far off stability, waits at the same magic number, and beta-decays back to a lower mass. That offset, repeated at N = 82 and N = 126, is the fingerprint that says there are two processes and not one

outputs.name: peak_offset_N82
outputs.doc: and at neutron number 82: 138 against 130

outputs.name: peak_offset_N126
outputs.doc: and at 126: lead-208 against platinum-195, thirteen apart

outputs.name: solar_metal_fraction
outputs.doc: 1.34 per cent of the Sun by mass is anything heavier than helium. Everything this laboratory is about is that one and a third per cent

instruments.title: The ladder — from a triangle to two Hubble constants

inputs.name: parallax_mas
inputs.doc: the measured angle, in milliarcseconds. Proxima Centauri is 768.5 and the Galactic centre is 0.125, which is the whole dynamic range of the technique in two numbers

inputs.name: astrometric_sigma_mas
inputs.doc: the astrometric precision. Gaia reaches about twenty microarcseconds at G = 15, and this is what decides where rung one has to hand over to rung two

inputs.name: cepheid_period_days
inputs.doc: the pulsation period of a classical Cepheid. Longer means brighter, which is the entire content of Leavitt`s law and the reason the method works at all

inputs.name: cepheid_apparent_magnitude
inputs.doc: and how bright it looks. A period gives the absolute magnitude, an apparent magnitude gives the distance, and the difference between them is the whole rung

inputs.name: zero_point_shift_mag
inputs.doc: a systematic shift applied to the ladder`s zero point, in magnitudes. This is the knob the whole subject turns on: 0.166 magnitudes anywhere below the top would make the two Hubble constants the same number, and the entire quoted error budget of all three rungs is 0.093

inputs.name: extinction_mag
inputs.doc: dust, which makes a thing fainter and therefore apparently further, and which does NOT cancel between rungs the way a random error does

inputs.name: limiting_magnitude
inputs.doc: how faint the telescope can go, which sets how far the type Ia rung reaches

outputs.name: parsec_from_au
outputs.doc: the parsec DERIVED from the astronomical unit rather than typed in: AU over the tangent of one arcsecond. It reproduces the tabulated value to eight parts per billion, because it is a definition — and this is the only place in the atlas where an AU is consumed at all

outputs.name: small_angle_error_ppb
outputs.doc: what dropping the tangent costs: eight parts per trillion. Small enough to ignore and measured rather than assumed, which is the difference between knowing and hoping

outputs.name: distance_pc
outputs.doc: the distance in parsecs, from the parallax alone. No photometry, no calibration, no model — a triangle

outputs.name: distance_ly
outputs.doc: and in light years, which is the same number wearing different units

outputs.name: parallax_reach_10pc_error
outputs.doc: how far the declared astrometric precision still gives a ten per cent distance, in parsecs. At Gaia`s twenty microarcseconds it is five kiloparsecs, which does not reach the Magellanic Clouds — and that gap is exactly why there is a second rung

outputs.name: parallax_reach_1pc_error
outputs.doc: and for one per cent it is five hundred parsecs

outputs.name: cepheid_absolute_magnitude
outputs.doc: what Leavitt`s law says the Cepheid IS, given its period and the zero point in force

outputs.name: cepheid_distance_pc
outputs.doc: and therefore how far away it is. Run this at a Cepheid in the Large Magellanic Cloud and it returns 49.7 kiloparsecs against the 49.6 the literature quotes

outputs.name: distance_modulus
outputs.doc: m minus M: the ladder`s only currency above the first rung, and the reason a systematic is ADDITIVE and travels upward unchanged

outputs.name: type_ia_reach_mpc
outputs.doc: how far a standardised type Ia stays above the limiting magnitude, in megaparsecs. At m = 25 it is seven thousand, which is redshift 1.8 and is why this rung reaches cosmology at all

outputs.name: ladder_random_mag
outputs.doc: the three rungs` random errors in quadrature

outputs.name: ladder_systematic_mag
outputs.doc: and their systematics added LINEARLY, because each rung is calibrated on the one below and a shift there is common to everything above. Which of these two you use is the difference between a three-sigma tension and a five-sigma one

outputs.name: ladder_total_distance_error
outputs.doc: the two combined, as a fractional distance error: 4.4 per cent

outputs.name: hubble_tension_sigma
outputs.doc: how far apart the two Hubble constants are in units of their combined uncertainty: 4.8. Neither number is computed here; both are quoted, and this is

outputs.name: hubble_tension_percent
outputs.doc: and as a fraction: 7.95 per cent

outputs.name: reconciling_systematic_mag
outputs.doc: THE NUMBER THIS LABORATORY EXISTS TO PRINT: how large a magnitude systematic would have to be hiding somewhere below the top for the two Hubble constants to be the same measurement. It is 0.166

outputs.name: systematic_over_budget
outputs.doc: and that number divided by the ladder`s ENTIRE quoted error budget, random and systematic together: 1.78. There is not room in the stated errors for the tension, which is the difference between a discrepancy and a crisis

outputs.name: hubble_constant_late
outputs.doc: the late-time value this ladder arrives at, quoted as a calibration

outputs.name: hubble_constant_early
outputs.doc: and the early-time value the microwave background gives, for the comparison above it

outputs.name: shifted_h0
outputs.doc: and the late-universe Hubble constant after the declared zero-point shift is applied. Turn the shift to 0.166 and it lands on Planck`s value exactly, which is the check that the arithmetic is the arithmetic

instruments.title: Where stars live — and the ratio a galaxy hangs on

inputs.name: population_age
inputs.doc: how old the stellar population is. This is the input the whole laboratory turns on: the mass-to-light ratio is not a number but a function of it, moving by a factor of sixty between a hundred million years and thirteen billion

inputs.name: stellar_mass
inputs.doc: a single star`s mass in solar masses, for the per-star quantities. Below 0.08 nothing ignites and above about 120 the star tears itself apart

inputs.name: imf
inputs.doc: which initial mass function. It matters by 44 per cent in the mass-to-light ratio, because the light comes from the top of the distribution and the mass from the bottom, and the two prescriptions disagree about the bottom

inputs.name: core_fraction
inputs.doc: what fraction of the star`s hydrogen is in the core and therefore burnable. This is the one genuinely soft number in the nuclear clock — the 0.7 per cent mass defect is measured, the c^2 is exact, and this is a modelling choice that scales every lifetime linearly

inputs.name: giant_window_fraction
inputs.doc: a giant-branch model, OFF by default. Stars within this fraction of the turnoff lifetime past the turnoff are treated as giants. Turn it on with the brightening below and watch the mass-to-light ratio collapse: the point of exposing it is that reasonable-looking parameters move the answer by a factor of nine, which is why the published ratio does not use it

inputs.name: giant_brightening
inputs.doc: how many times the turnoff luminosity a giant shines at, in that model

inputs.name: imf_samples
inputs.doc: quadrature points across nine decades of mass. The integrand has kinks at the mass-luminosity breakpoints, so the answer wobbles at the tenth of a per cent level rather than converging smoothly, and that is reported rather than smoothed away

outputs.name: luminosity
outputs.doc: the star`s luminosity. THIS UNIT IS THE REASON THE LABORATORY EXISTS: three benches in this atlas published a luminosity in watts and across a hundred and six laboratories nothing had ever consumed one

outputs.name: luminosity_solar
outputs.doc: and in solar units, which is how it is always quoted

outputs.name: mass_luminosity_exponent
outputs.doc: the LOCAL slope d ln L / d ln M, measured by differencing the relation rather than declared. It is 2.3, 4, 3.5 and 1 in four regimes, and quoting a single exponent costs orders of magnitude at the ends

outputs.name: effective_temperature
outputs.doc: from Stefan-Boltzmann given the luminosity and the radius — not a free parameter

outputs.name: stellar_radius
outputs.doc: in solar radii, from an EMPIRICAL fit and not from any theory here

outputs.name: main_sequence_lifetime
outputs.doc: eps f M c^2 / L. For the Sun it is ten billion years and for a sixty-solar-mass star three hundred thousand

outputs.name: eddington_luminosity
outputs.doc: 4 pi G M c / kappa: the luminosity at which a star pushes its own outer layers off

outputs.name: eddington_ratio
outputs.doc: the star`s luminosity as a fraction of that. The Sun is at 2.6e-5; a sixty-solar-mass star is at 0.83, and THAT is why the mass-luminosity exponent falls to one at the top — the ceiling is linear in mass, so the sequence that presses against it must be too

outputs.name: turnoff_mass
outputs.doc: the mass whose lifetime equals the population age, found by bisection on the clock. At ten billion years it is 1.01 solar masses, which is why the Sun is the canonical example of a star at its own turnoff

outputs.name: mass_to_light
outputs.doc: THE NUMBER THE GALAXY LABORATORY HANGS ON, in solar units: total mass ever born over the light of everything still alive. It is 0.19 at a hundred million years and 12 at thirteen billion — a factor of sixty — so a rotation-curve decomposition that quotes a mass-to-light ratio has quoted an AGE without saying so

outputs.name: mass_to_light_no_remnants
outputs.doc: and the same with the dead stars forgotten, which is the commonest way to get it wrong. At thirteen billion years the remnants are 14 per cent of the mass and carry no light at all

outputs.name: remnant_mass_fraction
outputs.doc: how much of the population`s mass is white dwarfs, neutron stars and black holes

outputs.name: giant_light_ratio
outputs.doc: under the declared giant model, the light of the giants divided by the light of the whole main sequence. Zero when the model is off. With a tenth-of-a-lifetime window and hundredfold brightening it is EIGHT, which is the measurement that justifies refusing to publish a corrected ratio

outputs.name: mass_to_light_with_giants
outputs.doc: and what the ratio would become if that model were believed. It is reported so the swing is visible and it is NOT the headline number

outputs.name: sun_lifetime_check
outputs.doc: the Sun`s own main-sequence lifetime from the same clock, unaffected by any input here. It must come out near ten billion years or the normalisation has drifted

instruments.title: The mass you can see is not the mass that is there

inputs.name: galaxy
inputs.doc: which galaxy to decompose

inputs.name: galactocentric_radius
inputs.doc: how far out to evaluate the decomposition. It is NOT called `radius`: this atlas has now measured three times what a generic coordinate name costs on the quantity bus, and a galaxy`s radius would have been proposed into an accretion disk and a stellar interior on the strength of the word alone

inputs.name: stellar_mass_multiplier
inputs.doc: a multiplier on the STELLAR mass, on top of whatever mass-to-light ratio the source paper adopted. This is the single largest freedom in the subject and the honest way to expose it is a knob: turn it up until the disc alone fits the inner curve and watch what it does to the outer one. The gas mass does not move, because a 21 cm line is a mass and not a luminosity. IT WAS CALLED mass_to_light FOR EXACTLY ONE RELEASE. The main-sequence laboratory then published an output of that name — an ABSOLUTE ratio of 9.4 in solar units where this is a multiplier of 1 — and the quantity bus proposed the coupling on the strength of the shared name and the shared absence of a unit. Same words, same dimensions, and a factor of nine between the meanings. The refusal is written in HCC_NOT_LINKS and this rename is what stops it recurring

inputs.name: halo_model
inputs.doc: which halo to fit to the leftover. NFW has a cusp at the centre and comes out of simulations; the pseudo-isothermal has a core and is what dwarf galaxies prefer. That disagreement has a name and is not settled here

inputs.name: halo_scale_radius
inputs.doc: r_s for NFW, r_c for the isothermal sphere

inputs.name: acceleration_scale
inputs.doc: a0. MOND fits this to rotation curves and gets 1.2e-10; the normalisation of the baryonic Tully-Fisher relation independently requires 1.6e-10, and the laboratory publishes both rather than adopting one

inputs.name: hubble_constant
inputs.doc: H0, so that a0 can be compared with c H0 / 2 pi. The cosmological-constant laboratory declares the same number and this one recomputes rather than imports it

outputs.name: v_disc
outputs.doc: the speed the stellar disc alone would produce at that radius, by Freeman`s closed form and not by sqrt(GM/r) — which at two kiloparsecs in NGC 3198 would say 254 against the disc`s 101

outputs.name: v_gas
outputs.doc: and the neutral hydrogen, with the helium correction, on its own longer scale length — which is why it keeps contributing where the starlight has run out

outputs.name: v_baryons
outputs.doc: the two in quadrature: everything anyone has ever seen

outputs.name: v_observed
outputs.doc: and what the 21 cm line actually says

outputs.name: v_halo_required
outputs.doc: the difference, in quadrature: the speed something invisible would have to supply

outputs.name: v_halo_model
outputs.doc: and what the CHOSEN profile supplies there, having been pinned once at the galaxy`s outermost measured point and given no further freedom. Where it parts from v_halo_required the SHAPE is wrong, not the amount — which is the whole content of the cusp-versus-core argument, and turning the scale radius is how to see it

outputs.name: missing_mass_factor
outputs.doc: the ratio of the dynamical mass to the baryonic one inside that radius. For NGC 3198 at thirty kiloparsecs it is 3.3 with the gas counted and 5.2 without, and the difference between those two numbers is why the gas is counted

outputs.name: mass_baryons
outputs.doc: v_bar^2 r / G

outputs.name: mass_dynamical
outputs.doc: v_obs^2 r / G

outputs.name: g_baryons
outputs.doc: the acceleration the visible mass produces there

outputs.name: g_observed
outputs.doc: and the acceleration actually observed. Plotting one against the other across many galaxies gives a single curve — the radial acceleration relation — which is the fact both explanations have to account for

outputs.name: g_mond
outputs.doc: what the simple interpolating function turns g_baryons into, at the declared a0

outputs.name: disc_peak_over_scale_length
outputs.doc: where the stellar disc`s own curve peaks, in scale lengths. It is 2.15 for every exponential disc that has ever existed, whatever its mass — a pure number, and the check that the Bessel functions are right

outputs.name: btfr_slope_free
outputs.doc: the slope of log M_b against log v_flat, fitted over the eight galaxies with nothing held fixed. It comes out 3.53, and a hundred galaxies give 3.9 — which is a statement about eight points and heterogeneous mass-to-light ratios, not about galaxies

outputs.name: btfr_normalisation
outputs.doc: and the normalisation with the slope held at 4, in solar masses per (km/s)^4. Fitted here from eight galaxies typed in by hand: 46.5, against the 47 published from a hundred

outputs.name: btfr_normalisation_from_a0
outputs.doc: what MOND requires that number to be, from 1/(G a0) alone: 62.8 at a0 = 1.2e-10

outputs.name: a0_implied_by_btfr
outputs.doc: and running it the other way: the acceleration scale the fitted relation implies, 1.62e-10. Two determinations of one constant, a third apart, both called a0

outputs.name: disc_scale_length
outputs.doc: the exponential scale length of the disc this decomposition is of, from the source paper`s own fit

outputs.name: acceleration_scale
outputs.doc: the a0 the run used, echoed back — what the answer was computed with is part of the answer

outputs.name: galaxy
outputs.doc: which galaxy answered, returned rather than assumed

outputs.name: a0_over_cH0_2pi
outputs.doc: a0 divided by c H0 / 2 pi, using this laboratory`s own H0. It is 1.15, which is either the deepest hint in the subject or numerology, and computing it is not deciding it

instruments.title: The planets of other stars — a transit, a wobble, and a zone

inputs.name: system
inputs.doc: which system to compute

inputs.name: impact_parameter
inputs.doc: b, how far off centre the planet crosses, in stellar radii. Past 1 + Rp/R* there is no transit at all and the laboratory says so rather than returning a number

inputs.name: albedo
inputs.doc: the Bond albedo used for the equilibrium temperature. Zero is the convention most catalogues quote; Earth`s is 0.306 and moves its equilibrium temperature from 278 K to 254 K

inputs.name: curve_samples
inputs.doc: how finely to trace the light curve

outputs.name: semi_major_axis_au
outputs.doc: a, from the period and the masses by Kepler III — computed from the measured GM and never from G times a mass in kilograms

outputs.name: depth_ppm
outputs.doc: the transit depth in parts per million. Earth across the Sun is 84 of them

outputs.name: depth_percent
outputs.doc: and as a percentage, which is the useful unit for a giant planet

outputs.name: duration_hours
outputs.doc: how long the planet is in front

outputs.name: transit_probability
outputs.doc: (R* + R_p)/a: the chance that a randomly oriented orbit is seen edge-on enough to transit at all. For the Earth it is one in two hundred, which is why a survey must watch a hundred thousand stars to find anything

outputs.name: transits
outputs.doc: 1 when the requested impact parameter actually produces a transit, 0 when the planet misses the disc

outputs.name: radial_velocity_ms
outputs.doc: K, the reflex speed of the star. Jupiter moves the Sun at a brisk walk and the Earth at nine centimetres a second

outputs.name: equilibrium_temperature
outputs.doc: T_eq at the requested albedo

outputs.name: flux_earth
outputs.doc: the starlight the planet receives, in units of what Earth receives. This is the quantity the habitable-zone criteria are actually written in and it is the one that survives disagreement about the star

outputs.name: luminosity_sun
outputs.doc: the star`s luminosity from its radius and temperature, in solar units

outputs.name: hz_inner_au
outputs.doc: the runaway-greenhouse edge, conservative

outputs.name: hz_outer_au
outputs.doc: the maximum-greenhouse edge, conservative

outputs.name: hz_optimistic_inner_au
outputs.doc: the recent-Venus edge

outputs.name: hz_optimistic_outer_au
outputs.doc: the early-Mars edge

outputs.name: in_conservative_zone
